title: Introduction to Java
description: Learn the basics of Java programming.

content.content: In this lesson, we will cover basic Java syntax and how to print to the console.

test.question: Write a Java program to print Hello, World! on the output
test.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println("Hello, World!"); } }

title: Java Variables and Data Types
description: Learn how to declare variables and use basic data types in Java.

content.content: In this lesson, we will learn about Java variables and data types.

test.question: Declare an integer variable 'age' with value 30 and print it.
test.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { int age = 30; System.out.println(age); } }

title: Java Conditional Statements
description: Learn how to use if-else statements in Java.

content.content: In this lesson, we will learn how to use if-else statements to control the flow of execution.

test.question: Write a Java program to check if a number is positive or negative.
test.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { int number = -5; if (number > 0) { System.out.println("Positive Number"); } else { System.out.println("Negative Number"); } } }

title: For Loops in Java
description: Learn how to use for loops to repeat actions.

content.content: In this lesson, we'll learn about for loops in Java. A for loop allows you to execute a block of code multiple times. It's especially useful when you want to perform an action a specific number of times. The for loop has three parts: initialization, condition, and increment/decrement.

test.question: Write a program that prints numbers from 1 to 5 using a for loop. Each number should be on a new line.
